title: Draw lines with an integer error accumulator
audience: Students with basic programming knowledge who are new to assembly
prerequisites: Signed comparisons and retained delayed branches
learningObjectives: Normalize endpoint order and specify ties
Implement independent coordinate decisions using a frozen doubled error
Handle steep, negative, axis-aligned, and point cases
Preserve a preexisting image and compare equivalent rasterizers

steps.title: Choose cells rather than continuous positions

quiz.prompt: Why does the default line have six cells?

choices.text: Its major-axis difference is five and both endpoints are included.
Every line always has six cells.
Its RGB word contains six hexadecimal digits.

hints.text: Count inclusive x positions from one through six.

steps.title: Read the frame and input contract

quiz.prompt: What should happen to a cell outside the selected line?

choices.text: It must always become black.
It must keep its complete original word.
Only its red byte must survive.

hints.text: This operation overlays a line rather than clearing an image.
An 8 by 8 frame uses 64 words, or 256 bytes.

quiz.prompt: What is the offset of x1 in this four-word block?

choices.text: One byte.
Four bytes.
Eight bytes.

hints.text: The third field starts after two four-byte words.
`$s0`,`$s1` hold the first point; `$s2`,`$s3` hold the second. The default is 1,1,6,4.

quiz.prompt: Why normalize endpoints?

choices.text: It fixes a common direction for deterministic halfway decisions.
It changes the RGB color.
It makes every line horizontal.

hints.text: A halfway cell choice can depend on the direction in which a naïve loop walks.
(6,4) to (1,1) is reordered to (1,1) to (6,4). Equal-x inputs are ordered upward in numeric y.

quiz.prompt: Why must the swap exchange both coordinates?

choices.text: Only x ever affects a pixel address.
Each x must remain paired with its original y.
Swapping y clears the canvas.

hints.text: Treat an endpoint as a pair, not as two unrelated values.
At `ordered`, x0 is no greater than x1. When x is equal, y0 is no greater than y1. Source memory is unchanged.

quiz.prompt: Which quantity is preserved as the endpoint target?

choices.text: The address scratch register.
The changing error value.
The ordered second coordinate pair.

hints.text: Separate the cursor from the destination.
Coordinates and error change; endpoint targets, differences, direction, frame base, and color stay fixed.

steps.title: Compute horizontal and signed vertical differences

quiz.prompt: Can the ordered horizontal difference be negative?

choices.text: No, because endpoint ordering made x0 no greater than x1.
Yes, for every steep line.
Only for a white color.

hints.text: Use the ordering invariant established before subtraction.
The default horizontal difference is five and signed vertical difference is three.

quiz.prompt: Why retain a separate y direction?

choices.text: The magnitude must keep a negative sign.
The distance magnitude alone cannot say whether y increases or decreases.
All negative slopes are out of bounds.

hints.text: Compare (1,1) to (6,4) with (1,6) to (6,3).
`$s5` is the vertical magnitude D; `$s6` is +1 or −1. For the default they are three and one.

quiz.prompt: What is the default initial error?

choices.text: Eight.
Negative eight.
Two.

hints.text: Substitute the differences into dx − D.
For dx=5 and D=3, dy is −3 and err is two.

steps.title: Load the fixed frame base and color

quiz.prompt: Which address stays fixed across every pixel?

choices.text: The frame base.
The address of the currently selected cell.
The running error interpreted as a pointer.

hints.text: Only the offset changes as the selected coordinates change.
`$t8` is 0x10010000 and `$t9` is the default white word 0x00ffffff.

quiz.prompt: Why shift the cell index left by two?

choices.text: To double the error for a branch.
Each framebuffer cell occupies four bytes.
The board has two rows.

hints.text: Distinguish a cell count from a byte address.
For (1,1), the cell index is nine and the address is 0x10010024.

quiz.prompt: Which point has been painted at the first `pixel_written` hit?

choices.text: The final endpoint only.
The next point after an update.
The current ordered starting point.

hints.text: The coordinate updates appear later in the program.
The first default cell is white; the other 63 words keep their previous values.

quiz.prompt: Why test after the store?

choices.text: To include the final endpoint and the one-point case.
To force an extra pixel beyond every line.
To clear the input first.

hints.text: Consider what a pre-store exit would do when the endpoints are identical.
Coincident endpoints paint one cell and exit without a coordinate update.

quiz.prompt: Why save this value separately?

choices.text: The color instruction needs it as an address.
The first update can change err before the second decision.
MIPS forbids comparing the same register twice.

hints.text: The two conditions belong to one decision state, not two successive ones.
`$t2` is four on the first default update and remains four through both coordinate decisions.

quiz.prompt: Which value does the next decision still use?

choices.text: The new error doubled again.
The pixel color.
The saved doubled error from before this x update.

hints.text: A temporary protects the original decision input.
For the first default update, x becomes two and err becomes −1; the saved e2 is still four.

quiz.prompt: Can both x and y step in one update?

choices.text: Yes; diagonal progress requires both independent conditions.
No; one condition must always exclude the other.
Only when the color is zero.

hints.text: Evaluate both default inequalities with e2 four, dy −3, and dx five.
The first update finishes at (2,2), err four, with the original e2 still four.

quiz.prompt: What keeps a delay slot from painting an extra cell here?

choices.text: Delay slots never execute.
The slot is explicitly `nop`.
The display ignores the final instruction.

hints.text: Inspect the instruction immediately following the branch.
The default final image contains six white cells, with every off-line word preserved.

quiz.prompt: What does an error value of zero mean here?

choices.text: The entire program must stop.
The pixel is black.

hints.text: Termination is a coordinate comparison, not an error comparison.

The x and y decisions can independently skip or take a step.
The framebuffer rotates automatically.

hints.text: Look for an update in which only the y condition is true.

quiz.prompt: Why does a black-background-only test miss errors?

choices.text: Black is not a legal color.
All cells share one memory address.
A program that clears unrelated cells could accidentally pass.

hints.text: Choose preexisting values that make unwanted writes visible.
Selected cells become the exact color word; every other word and all inputs remain unchanged.

quiz.prompt: Why is err not simply the perpendicular distance in pixels?

hints.text: Track the coefficients of i and j rather than assigning physical units by appearance.
